ns2:section.sectionText: "A HISTORY OF POPULAR MUSIC IN JAPAN." From the films of Hayao Miyazaki to cult anime classics and Harajuku street fashion, a fascination with Japanese popular culture continues to be a seemingly global phenomenon. This course will look at one of Japan’s largest pillars of “soft power”: popular music. In understanding how the mainstream industry developed from the post-WWII period until the present day, we will take a journey from the earliest forms of commercial entertainment in the 17th century. Tracing these much earlier origins, we will complicate notions of “the popular” and Japan’s relationship to Western theories of musical practice in the 19th and 20th centuries. From medieval street musicians, kabuki players, and singing puppeteers to Shina Ringo and Kyary Pamyu Pamyu, this course offers an expansive survey of popular music in Japan and its relationship to broader social, cultural, and economic histories. A background in music, although considered advantageous, will not be a prerequisite for this course. Students outside of the School of Music are therefore encouraged to enroll.
